names.note: Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 19 марта ст. ст., name page 14691, «Симеон Дайбабский, прп.», with the rank word left off. The day's own line declines it the same way. The form is the Russian calendar's own spelling of the Serbian Дајбабе; no Serbian source was read for this folder.

death.note: The year days.pravoslavie.ru closes his line with for 19 марта ст. ст.: «Прп. Симеона Дайбабского (1941) (Серб.).» It is the only year the calendar gives him, and neither the day page nor name page 14691 carries a life.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 марта ст. ст. — «Прп. Симеона Дайбабского (1941) (Серб.).»

attestations.note: Neither the day page nor name page 14691 carries a life, and the day page prints no hymn for him. The line marks him «(Серб.)», a saint of the Serbian church whom this Russian calendar keeps; the name page lists a second day, «30 августа (Серб.)», which is presumably the Serbian church's own, and it is recorded here. **That day page was read and he is owed no row for it** (read 14 October 2026): what 30 августа keeps is «Собор святителей Сербских», which ENUMERATES thirteen Serbian hierarchs by name — Саввы I, Арсения I, Саввы II, Евстафия I, Иакова, Никодима, Даниила, Иоанникия II, Ефрема II, Спиридона, Макария, Гавриила I and Григория, each with his own name link — and he is not among them, being a монах dead in 1941 and not a hierarch, with no line and no name link on that page. An enumerating synaxis is one row for each man it names; he is not named, so the day is a feast of a company he does not belong to. **The serbian row of this folder is `undocumented` and the Serbian calendar was not read**, so a Serbian reader coming to 30 August will meet him already here and should put the Serbian row on whichever day pravoslavno.rs prints.
